task.description: Rework: convert two disguised executable code snippets (an Enum.reduce anonymous-function fold, an Enum.filter field-selection expression) to pure prose, and do a fresh full re-scan for anything similar.

result.note: Fixed both required defects: line 312 (Enum.filter(& &1.queried) -> prose describing keeping only queried:true fields), line 489 (Enum.reduce fn c, acc -> dynamic(...) end -> prose describing a left fold ANDing each clause onto the accumulator from a true identity). Fresh re-scan additionally found and fixed two passages in sections 5.3/5.5 using bare arrow operator-to-expression mappings without the explicit conceptually/e.g. framing used elsewhere -- reworded both to lead with prose description, Elixir shown only as a parenthetical e.g. example, matching the validator's own already-accepted precedent style. Rigorous self-check: grepped for Enum./fn /def /defp /defmodule/case /cond /with /pipe/do-blocks/arrow-to-brace across the whole document -- no Enum.*, fn, defmodule, def, defp, cond, or pipe occurrences remain; all case/with hits are inert English prose, not Elixir syntax; the only remaining arrow hit is the pre-existing validator-accepted fragmentary case-arm illustration; all remaining single-expression Elixir fragments are now explicitly framed as conceptually/e.g. parenthetical illustrations of a prose-described shape, not standalone executable logic. @spec/@type fenced blocks unchanged.
